sets.title: Strong and weak ownership with atomic and non-atomic counts

objective_text.T66.06.a: Prove the distinct value/control lifetimes, no-resurrection property and count-overflow behavior; distinguish reference-count synchronization from pointee synchronization and cycle collection.
objective_text.T66.06.b: Implement strong/weak ownership twice, first under exclusion and then with C17 atomics, documenting initialization publication, owned-reference preconditions, callback effects and each memory-order edge.
objective_text.T66.06.c: Trace every strong/weak boundary with an independent counter model, test maximum-count refusal, and reject omission of the implicit weak release. Run the actual four-thread anchor, separate TSan if available, GCC/Clang optimized and ASan/UBSan builds, inspect atomic lowering and report lock-free status. A quiet race detector does not prove the memory-order argument or reclaim safety for fabricated references.

sets.title: A checked façade around a trusted core: bounded tenant-isolation failure

objective_text.T66.10.a: Derive the integer-wrap admission defect, attacker-controlled transition and exact violated authority property; distinguish a checked trusted-core boundary from whole-process memory safety.
objective_text.T66.10.b: Implement the subtraction-based boundary check, unchanged-on-failure behavior and an internal validated descriptor, preserving the simple core while documenting every remaining caller and same-process assumption.
objective_text.T66.10.c: Run the local cross-tenant demonstration with synthetic canaries, compare flawed/repaired outcomes, enumerate all ordinary tenant/offset/count combinations around8 and test UINT_MAX wrap cases. Reject the flawed-check mutant by a normal semantic assertion. Explain why ASan may remain quiet: every actual array access is in bounds. Test mitigation regression without claiming arbitrary code execution or privilege escalation.
objective_text.T66.10.d: Move the descriptor across an FFI or serialized boundary: reject fabricated fields and revalidate at that boundary rather than trusting a C typedef. Delayed assessment separates read from write capabilities and allows a read-only subview; derive authority attenuation and test that subview construction cannot widen rights.
